models_evaluated: four LLM platforms (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Guideline alignment and pharmacotherapeutic accuracy of LLM-generated simulations judged by expert panels
links.effect: Clinical accuracy and safety was the limiting domain (58.3%) versus clinical reasoning (81.6%) and instructional design (82.5%). Guideline misalignment and pharmacotherapeutic inaccuracies found; 53 of 103 sessions passed all domains.
links.quote: Clinical accuracy and safety emerged as the limiting domain (58.3%) compared to clinical reasoning (81.6%) and instructional design (82.5%).

links.outcome: Presence of fabricated evidence in LLM-generated simulation sessions
links.effect: Error analysis found fabricated evidence, along with guideline misalignment, pharmacotherapeutic inaccuracies and cross-condition therapeutic recommendations, occurring exclusively in AML sessions.
links.quote: Error analysis revealed guideline misalignment, pharmacotherapeutic inaccuracies, fabricated evidence, and cross-condition therapeutic recommendations occurring exclusively in AML sessions.

unlisted_practices: Expert-guided meta-prompts for generating LLM educational simulations
Expert panel review of LLM-generated educational content before use in pharmacy education
Platform-specific and disease-specific validation of LLM educational tools

screen.reason: Empirical mixed-methods evaluation of LLM-generated clinical simulations for pharmacy students, measuring clinical accuracy, safety, and student perception without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
